title: fix: polli usage --daily asks for 7 days by default
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- `polli usage --daily` now asks for the last 7 days instead of the endpoint's 90-day default. `--days N` still sets any window.
- Why: on heavy accounts the 90-day query times out in Tinybird (20 s limit) and the CLI shows a 500. Seven days takes about 6 s on a test account with ~570k requests a day.
- Bumps polli-cli to 0.1.29.

Addresses #16560. The endpoint itself stays slow for very heavy accounts: read-time dedup over ~28M rows takes 15–20 s. Duplicates are real (8.8M rows in January), so the pipe fix is a separate change.

gist.headline: Seven days, fewer timeouts
gist.blurb: Polli’s daily usage view takes a shorter stroll through the calendar. The 90-day hike is still available with `--days N`.
gist.summary: polli-cli 0.1.29 changes `polli usage --daily` to request seven days instead of the endpoint’s 90-day default, avoiding a Tinybird timeout on heavy accounts while preserving `--days N` for custom windows.
gist.impact: Heavy accounts get a more reliable daily usage report by default; the seven-day query took about six seconds on a test account with roughly 570,000 requests per day.
